title: Conditional mutual information under a.e. change of both arguments
statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a sample space $\Omega$, and let $X, X' \colon \Omega \to S$, $Y, Y' \colon \Omega \to T$, and $Z \colon \Omega \to U$ be measurable maps into countable spaces, each taking only finitely many values $\mu$-almost surely. If $X = X'$ and $Y = Y'$ hold $\mu$-almost everywhere, then the conditional mutual informations agree:
\[
I[X : Y \mid Z\,;\,\mu] \;=\; I[X' : Y' \mid Z\,;\,\mu].
\]
hypotheses_covered: X, Y, Z, X', Y' measurable into countable spaces
each of X, Y, Z, X', Y' has finite range
replaced:
Under a probability measure, if $X =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} X'$ and $Y =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} Y'$,
then $I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] = I[X' : Y' \mid Z;\mu]$ (the conditioning variable $Z$ is
unchanged).
